articles.text:
5. basu (バス) 'bus'

Japanese buses are equipped with a tape of the pre-recorded names of their stops which is set to announce, at the appropriate time, the name of the next stop.

In most cases, you pay as you enter a bus. It is advisable that you have the exact change, although there is a money exchange machine which exchanges a hundred yen coin for ten yen coins (you can't use a bill). The fares are usually in units of 100 yen and 10 yen. If you don't know the fare, you can ask the driver by saying:

(your destination) made ikura desu ka?

Kaisuu-ken (回数券) 'coupon tickets' and teeki-ken (定期券) 'season pass' are also available, but these can't be bought on a bus. You have to go to a ticket window at the main bus terminal. There is no free ticket transfer system.
